slides.title: Welcoming international students
slides.subtitle: Simple ways to be a friend in the first few weeks
slides.notes: Welcome people as they arrive. Invite them to sit with someone they don't know yet.

points.title: What it feels like to arrive

points: Think back to a time you were the newcomer. What helped you feel welcome?
prompts: What did they say or do?
slides.notes: Ask: Think back... Give people a minute of quiet first. Listen for: small, practical gestures. Transition: 'Students feel this every day for months.'

slides.title: What the first weeks can feel like
Small things that make a big difference
points: Learn how to say their name well
Offer a ride from the airport or to the store
Invite them for a meal at your home
Ask about their family and home country

slides.question: What might make a student hesitate to accept an invitation?
slides.notes: Listen for: language worries, food, not wanting to be a burden, cultural norms about hospitality.

slides.story: Mei has been on campus for two weeks. You meet her at a welcome event. She smiles but answers your questions with one or two words, and keeps checking her phone.
slides.question: What would you do?
options: Ask a few more questions to keep the conversation going
Share a little about yourself first
Invite her to the next event and give her space
Introduce her to another student from her country
slides.notes: Show of hands for each option. There isn't one right answer; ask people to explain why they chose it.

slides.title: A first conversation
steps: One person plays a newly arrived student
One person starts a friendly conversation
One person observes and takes notes

points: What surprised you in the practice?
Which question opened up the conversation most?
What would you do differently next time?

slides.title: Let's take a break
slides.text: Coffee and tea are at the back.

points: Arriving is hard, even for confident students
Good questions open doors; listen more than you talk
slides.next_step: Invite one international student for coffee **this week**.

slides.title: Thank you!
slides.subtitle: What questions are still on your mind?
